page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 40 virtual CPUs derived from 20 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.8 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge demonstrates solid mid-range performance. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance processes Redis SET operations at 34.78 million operations per second and handles static web serving throughput at 25.35 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds reach 1841.39 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model, and 56.94 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio offer predictable performance for enterprise workloads without the overhead of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This hardware profile is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale machine learning inference tasks that do not require GPU acceleration.
